input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting this fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my phone’s internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else.

Oh, I see. My phone is in airplane mode right now, and it looks like there’s no service. Also, mobile data and data roaming are both turned off. What should I do next? I’m a bit nervous about changing settings—will this mess anything up?

Oh dear, I didn’t realize there was a bill overdue! If paying it will get my internet working again, then yes, please send me the payment request. Will I need to do anything complicated after I pay, or will my phone just start working again? I get worried about these things.

I’ve just completed the payment for the overdue bill. What should I do next? Will my phone start working right away, or do I need to do something else? I’m a bit anxious about getting everything back to normal.
I restarted my phone, but it still shows that airplane mode is on at the top of the screen. Is there something else I should do? I’m worried I might mess something up.

Yes, please! I’d appreciate your help with that. I always get nervous about changing these settings—will turning off airplane mode affect anything else on my phone? I just want to make sure I don’t lose anything important, like my photos.

Okay, I’ve turned off airplane mode. Now I see a signal bar at the top, but it says “2G” and something about data being disabled. Is that normal? What should I do next? I really want to make sure my internet is excellent this time.

I’ve turned on mobile data and set the network to prefer 4G and 5G. Now the top of my screen shows “5G” with excellent signal, and data is enabled. Is there anything else I should do to make sure my internet is excellent? Should I test it somehow?

Oh, I tried to run a speed test, but it says there’s no connection. That’s confusing because it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top. What should I do now? I really need my internet to be excellent—anything less just won’t do.

It looks like Data Saver mode is turned on. Could that be stopping my internet from working properly? Should I turn it off, or is there something else I need to check? I just want to make sure I do this right.

I turned off Data Saver mode, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says there’s no connection. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working when it shows 5G and excellent signal? What should I do next?
It looks like there is a VPN turned on and connected on my phone. Could that be causing the problem? Should I turn it off? I’m not sure what a VPN even is, so I’d need some help with this.

Yes, I am currently abroad in France, so I guess roaming might be needed. I’d appreciate your help with both turning off the VPN and enabling roaming. I get nervous about these things—will doing this mess up anything else on my phone? I just want my internet to work perfectly.

I turned off the VPN and enabled roaming, but the speed test still says there’s no connection. I’m really starting to worry—why isn’t my internet working even though everything looks right at the top of my screen? What else can I try? I really need excellent internet speed.
Yes, please enable roaming on my line. I’m in France right now, so I think I need it. Will this finally get my internet working? I really hope so—I just want excellent speed!
I restarted my phone and ran the speed test again—this time it says the speed is excellent! Thank you so much for your help. I was really worried, but now everything seems to be working perfectly.
Thank you so much for your patience and help! I really appreciate it. I feel much better now. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
